target_customer: Consumers worried about contaminants and toxins in food and water
problem: Consumers cannot cheaply test food or water for toxins; lab spectroscopy is expensive and not portable.
business_model: consumer hardware device with consumable nanoparticle substrates

founders.name: Victor Ng
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as software engineer; no other bio.

founders.name: Peter Xian
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no bio.

competitors.name: TellSpec
competitors.what: Handheld food scanner sending data to cloud analysis
competitors.traction_then: Expected on the market in early 2016

competitors.name: SCiO (Consumer Physics)
competitors.what: General handheld spectrometer for reading material composition

technical_complexity.rationale: Miniaturizing a Raman spectroscope to consumer cost and pairing it with proprietary nanoparticle substrates is hardware and materials research.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary substrates could protect the sensing method, but nothing shows a patent or working product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced evidence of incumbents copying or acquiring Silver.

market_need_then: In 2015 and 2016 several consumer food sensors (Nima, TellSpec, SCiO) drew pre-orders and press, though experts criticized TellSpec and SCiO for overstating abilities.

branding.domain_note: scansilver.com; it returned 503 when checked in 2026-11.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found and the one word name is generic.

outcome_analysis: Silver, a Winter 2016 company, set out to build the first miniaturized Raman spectroscope for consumers using nanoparticle substrates, and is listed Inactive. No shutdown notice, post-mortem, press coverage or follow-on funding was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. The hardware and materials problem was research grade, which is context rather than a sourced cause.
notes: The $120K total rests on CB Insights alone (Crunchbase shows no amount); the round date is approximate. The Raman and nanoparticle description comes from the YC page; Round Funded's reconstructed application text was not used. Location conflicts: YC says San Francisco, other sites say Cupertino. The CNBC article date and competitor descriptions come from a search snippet, not a full page fetch. Cause of inactivity not public.
